standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of cohomology of the cohomology sheaves on the objects of B and vanishing of R^1 lim
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the hypotheses (2)(a) and (2)(b) of the statement, which are the conditions under which cohomology of limits is computed by limits of cohomologies
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the two vanishing statements that make the limit exact.

core_obligations: Set up the exact sequence (proof lines 5521-5530): the author writes the long exact cohomology sequence relating the cohomology of the derived limit to the limit of the cohomologies and to the terms involving R^1 lim.

Apply the hypotheses (proof lines 5530-5538): hypothesis (2)(a) kills the cohomology of the cohomology sheaves in positive degrees on the objects of B, and hypothesis (2)(b) kills the R^1 lim terms, so the limit is exact and the identification H^q(R lim K_n) = lim H^q(K_n) follows, first on the objects of B and then everywhere because B covers every object.
proof_roadmap: Write the exact sequence relating the cohomology of the derived limit to the limit of the cohomologies.
Use the two vanishing hypotheses to make the limit exact.
Conclude the identification on B and hence on the whole site.
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the cohomology sheaves of a derived limit with the limits of the cohomology sheaves, under the hypothesis that the cohomology of the cohomology sheaves vanishes in positive degrees on the objects of B and that the associated inverse systems have vanishing R^1 lim (statement lines 5504-5519). The proof writes the exact sequence of the derived limit (proof lines 5521-5530) and uses the two vanishing hypotheses to kill the extra terms (proof lines 5530-5538), which yields the identification on the objects of B and hence everywhere. The non-formal content is the reading of the hypotheses as exactness of the limit. The claim is H2: one exact sequence plus two vanishing inputs.
